name: Democratic confederalism
summary: Democratic confederalism, developed by Abdullah Öcalan under the influence of Murray Bookchin, seeks a stateless, grass-roots democracy of local assemblies federated into larger councils, replacing the nation-state rather than capturing it. It puts women's liberation, ecology and a multi-ethnic, multi-religious society alongside a cooperative economy aimed at need rather than profit, and it holds self-defence to be a communal right.
scope: Democratic confederalism as Abdullah Öcalan sets it out in his Democratic Confederalism pamphlet (s1) and as the Kurdish Freedom Movement presents and practises it (s4, s5, s6): a stateless, directly democratic confederation of local assemblies, with women's liberation, ecology and a plural society. It excludes classic Kurdish nationalism and Bookchin's own libertarian municipalism, which s4 and s6 present as its source rather than the same doctrine.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: 'Democratic confederations will sustain self-defence forces at all times' (s1, III.H); Öcalan calls self-defence essential (III.E).

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: s1 holds confederations will keep self-defence forces against attacks and interventions by nation-states.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: s1 treats assimilation by the nation-state as violence against cultures, and democratic confederalism will not stand idly by assimilation efforts (III.H).

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: s1 (II.B.2) ties capitalist monopolism and its expansion to the wars of nation-states.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority is collective consensus in communal assemblies (s1, III); s1 (II.A.2, II.B.4) criticises clerical influence on power.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: s1 principle 5 leaves existing political borders alone and rejects the nation-state.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: s1 rejects hegemony and wars between nation-states, and treats diversity as strength.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Principle 3 of s1 says higher levels only coordinate and implement the will of the communities that send delegates, while basic decision power stays with local institutions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democracies 'rest on voluntary participation' while the state rests on coercion (s1, III); power stems from the communities.

corporate-influence.rationale: s1 (II.B.2) describes capital monopolies and the state as fused, controlling politics.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: s1 builds confederalism on equal coexistence of cultures and identities.

decide-locally.rationale: Öcalan's principle 3 puts basic decision power with the local grass-roots institutions; higher levels only coordinate and carry out what the communities decide (s1, section IV).

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy in Öcalan's sense is the aim, and s4 says outside democratic confederalism there is no people's government; neither speaks of voters choosing badly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: s1 says state office is legitimised in part by elections yet remains state power, and democracy needs strong participation; s4 calls democracy people's power, not a form of government.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: s4 says a state cannot be ended with a state, and Öcalan faults real socialism for falling into the trap of building a state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Öcalan treats sexism as an ideological pillar of the nation-state and women's equality as a central pillar of confederalism (s1, II.B.3, III).

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: s1 says cultural diversity strengthens a society's defences and monocultures are less robust (V.8), and builds confederalism on ethnic, cultural and political diversity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: s1 (II.A.2) criticises deriving state power from divine will; confederalism rests on collective consensus.

domination-women-nature.rationale: s6 reports the movement links domination of women with domination of nature, as does s1 (II.B.3).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: s1 criticises the UN as a union of nation-states led by superpowers and proposes a confederal assembly to oppose it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: s4 says Öcalan's democratic republic advocates democracy in the context of citizens' rights, and s1 asks for equal coexistence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Öcalan rejects the homogeneous national society as artificial, and s4 defines the democratic nation as a plural community not tied to a single language or religion.

experts-over-public.rationale: Decision power rests with the communities (s1, principle 3), and s4 defines democracy as the people's power; expert rule would contradict that.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: s6 and s4 present freedom as self-rule free from state and patriarchal domination.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Armed forces answer to democratic institutions, and the society decides their duties (s1, III.E), not a head of state.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: s1 says freedom needs change beyond forming a state, including the economy (principle 1, II.B.2).

indirect-election.rationale: Communities send delegates to general assemblies at higher levels, serving for a limited time as mouthpiece and executive (s1, principle 3); s4 describes assemblies built up from commune to city and region. Neither says the delegates choose officials, so low.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: s4: in the new paradigm violence has no role beyond legitimate self-defence; s1: democratic confederalism is at war with no nation-state.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: s1 (II.B.3) links sexism, nationalism, capitalism and state power as reinforcing each other.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: s1 rejects uniting a people in a single nation-state; an umbrella confederation across states is its answer.

language-defines-nation.rationale: s4 quotes Öcalan that no nation can be reduced to shared language, culture, market or history.

means-match-ends.rationale: s6 says Öcalan and Bookchin espouse a prefigurative politics, and s4 holds that a state cannot be ended by a state.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: s4: democratic autonomy for Kurdish regions within a unitary or federal state, with constitutional recognition of Kurdish identity.

municipal-property.rationale: s6 describes commons and communal ownership managed by communes.

nation-first.rationale: Öcalan calls democratic confederalism an anti-nationalist movement and proposes a global confederal assembly (s1, principle 5 and III.G).

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: s1 calls expressing one's cultural, ethnic or national identity a natural right, and s4 describes assemblies for ethnic, religious and cultural identities with democratic autonomy inside a unitary state.

national-self-determination.rationale: s1 principle 1: self-determination includes the right to a state of one's own, though founding one does not increase freedom.

natural-rulers.rationale: Politics is open to every stratum of society and decided in communal assemblies (s1, III.D); government by a naturally apt few contradicts this.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: s1, s6 and s4 reject both capitalism and state socialism for a communal, ecological economy.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Confederal self-administration is meant to run an alternative economy and ecology as well as defence (s1, III), so its government is not limited to protecting against violence.

one-party-rule.rationale: Democratic confederalism is 'open towards other political groups and factions' and has no room for hegemony, above all in ideology (s1, III and III.F).

participatory-democracy.rationale: Öcalan says democracy is grass-roots participation: all groups take part directly in local decisions, and 'politics becomes part of everyday life' (s1, III.D); s4 calls it people's power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Armed forces are under direct control of democratic institutions, and their leadership is set equally by political institutions and confederate groupings (s1, III.E); party command contradicts it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: s1 (II.B.3) says patriarchy and sexism pervade the whole society and keep women the most colonised group; s4 says Öcalan's analysis of women and the state is central.

people-in-arms.rationale: s6 reads Öcalan as calling for popular militias, an armed citizenry, beside the assemblies, though s1 keeps them under democratic control rather than abolishing every standing force.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Öcalan contrasts states founded on power with democracies 'based on collective consensus', calling democratic confederalism consensus-oriented (s1, III).

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: s4 says the movement foresees no role for violence beyond legitimate self-defence, which excludes violence as a general means of pursuing political goals.

population-transfer.rationale: s1 (V.8): no state has the right to drive people from their ancestral cultural region; ethnic cleansing is condemned.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: s1 (II.B.4) argues the state and capital shape science and ideology to serve power.

production-for-use.rationale: s1 and s6 describe an ecological, communal economy that serves social needs rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: s1 (II.B.2) describes capitalism as profit maximisation resting on exploitation of labour and nature.

property-franchise.rationale: s1: confederalism opens political space to all strata of society (III.D); a property franchise excludes most of them.

racial-franchise.rationale: s1 opens political space to all strata and identities (III.D); a franchise for one ethnic group contradicts it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: s1 asks for equal coexistence of peoples and rejects homogenising policy; a law enforcing segregation contradicts it.

religious-nation.rationale: s4 quotes Öcalan: the democratic nation is not tied to a single language, religion or reading of history.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: s1: no state has the right to drive people from their ancestral cultural region (V.8).

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: s1 condemns ethnic cleansing and the annihilation of minorities by nation-states (II.A.4, V.8).

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: s1 rules out a Kurdish nation-state and offers confederal structures across the four parts of Kurdistan without questioning existing borders.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: s1 and s4 seek a democratic solution for Kurds within existing borders, with no separate state.

sacred-nation.rationale: s1 (II.B.1) calls nationalism the religion of a quasi-divine nation-state, a justification for exploitation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: s1 (II.A.2) criticises the state's quasi-divine attributes and rulers by divine grace.

single-official-language.rationale: s1 rejects the nation-state's single culture and identity and s4 says the democratic nation is not tied to a single language.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Öcalan faults the nation-state for disarming society and monopolising force, and says confederalism involves no military monopoly (s1, II.A.2 and III.E).

state-class-instrument.rationale: s4 reports the state defined as an instrument of ruling-class oppression and Öcalan's analysis of it; s6 quotes him on the state as the collective means of protecting stolen property; s1 calls legal order the class rule of the bourgeoisie.

state-harmful.rationale: s4 says humanity must find a system free of the state and that only democratic confederalism can transcend it; s1 calls overcoming the state a long-term process and rejects both total rejection and complete recognition of it. Aim is stateless, not immediate abolition.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: s4: Öcalan holds that liberation cannot come through constructing a state and that real socialism fell into that trap.

strong-leader.rationale: Power is to rest with grass-roots councils and consensus; s1 (III.F) rejects hegemony and arbitrary bureaucratic decisions, which a leader bypassing deliberation would be.

suppress-opposition.rationale: s1 calls for understanding and respect for dissenting opinions and an open political space for all groups (III.D, III.F).

total-state.rationale: Öcalan faults the nation-state for aiming to monopolise all social processes (s1, II.A.4); s4 calls it totalitarian dominance seeking to rule society's very cells.

vanguard-party.rationale: s4 says Öcalan's paradigm turns to political organisation outside the party; s6 (sympathetic authors) calls the disciplined vanguard cadre a contradiction of the goal.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: s1 (II.B.2) says capital monopolies and the state concentrate power at society's expense.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: s1 ties women's liberation to dismantling the state and capitalist economy (II.B.3, III).

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: s4 describes autonomous women's organisations inside confederal structures.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's freedom and equality are a main pillar (s1, V.3) and all strata take part in politics (III.D).

notes: Answers rest on Öcalan's Democratic Confederalism (s1), Komun Academy (s4), Fitzherbert (s5) and Hammy & Miley (s6). Sources s2 (the 2014 Charter, which does not name the ideology) and s3 (Wikipedia, not evidence) are kept only because earlier answers' talk-page history cites them; no current answer does. 154 earlier answers resting on them or on inference were nulled. Themes searched: state and democracy, confederal structure, violence and self-defence, nation and ethnicity, religion, women and gender, ecology, economy and property. Statements on taxes, welfare, markets and many social issues stay null because the sources set out principles rather than programmes. Jacobin and Taylor & Francis pages could not be fetched.

keyFigures.role: Founder of the PKK and theorist of democratic confederalism
keyFigures.quote: Öcalan’s radical democracy is intrinsic to the concept of democratic confederalism which he borrowed from Murray Bookchin.
